official_sources: NPPF Annex 2 glossary MSA and MCA

official_measurement_examples.name: MSA purpose
official_measurement_examples.fact: Mineral Safeguarding Areas protect known mineral resources from needless sterilisation by non-mineral development; designation does not create a presumption that minerals will be worked.

official_measurement_examples.name: MCA distinction
official_measurement_examples.fact: A Mineral Consultation Area is a geography based on safeguarding where district or borough authorities should consult the Mineral Planning Authority on relevant non-mineral proposals; it is not the same legal concept as the MSA.

official_measurement_examples.name: Prior extraction context
official_measurement_examples.fact: Prior extraction can be encouraged where practical and environmentally feasible, but it is proposal-specific and not an automatic requirement for every safeguarded parcel.

official_measurement_examples.name: Planning and permits
official_measurement_examples.fact: Mineral extraction requires planning permission and may also need separate environmental or nature-related permits and licences.

official_measurement_examples.name: Resource mapping limitation
official_measurement_examples.fact: Mineral-resource or safeguarding geometry shows planning evidence and potential resource context, not ownership, reserve quantity or economic viability for an individual parcel.

official_measurement_examples.name: Non-mineral development
official_measurement_examples.fact: An MSA intersection does not automatically prohibit non-mineral development; policy tests, consultation and site-specific evidence determine the planning balance.

official_measurement_examples.name: Safeguarded infrastructure
official_measurement_examples.fact: Mineral policy also safeguards handling, processing and transport sites, which must remain distinct from in-ground mineral-resource polygons.

official_measurement_examples.name: Promotion guard
official_measurement_examples.fact: No parcel mineral clearance, reserve estimate or Future Growth score is promoted while recovery is parked.

core_rules: MSA is safeguarding not extraction permission
MCA is consultation geography distinct from MSA
safeguarding does not presume resource will be worked
mineral planning permission is distinct from other permits
resource mapping is not reserve quantity
MSA intersection is not automatic refusal
safeguarded infrastructure and in-ground resources remain distinct
no promotion while recovery is parked
source_verification_note: Official GOV.UK planning policy, legislation and BGS authoritative mineral-planning sources checked on 2026-07-26. MSA/MCA, prior extraction and permit distinctions were retained; no parcel promotion.
